function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Below is an up‑to‑date snapshot (as of May 2026) of key Texas traffic laws you’ll want to know if you’re driving—or even riding—through the Lone Star State. I’ve grouped them into categories so it’s easy to skim what matters most for everyday drivers, commercial operators, cyclists, pedestrians, and new residents who may still be adjusting from another state. --- ### 1️⃣ General Driving Rules | Rule | What It Means | Why It Matters | |------|---------------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | Posted limits vary by road type:
• Rural two‑lane roads – 55 mph
• Urban arterials – 45–65 mph depending on signage
• Highways/Interstates – 70–75 mph (except where posted otherwise)
*Texas allows “reasonable” speeds below posted limits.* | Exceeding limits triggers points & fines; under‑speeding can create hazards. | | **Seat Belt Law** | All occupants must wear seat belts. Drivers must buckle themselves before passengers do. Children <8 years old must ride rear‑seat in child safety seats unless they weigh ≥40 lbs *and* have a lap‑belt only. | Violations carry $50 fine + 2 points. Points lead to license suspension after 12 points within 36 months. | | **Hands‑Free Phone Use** | Texting, emailing, browsing, or using social media while driving is illegal. Voice calls via hands‑free devices are allowed. | Fines start at $100 plus 2 points. Repeat offenders face higher penalties. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) >0.08% is DUI. For commercial drivers, BAC limit is 0.04%. Penalties include jail time, license revocation, mandatory alcohol treatment programs. | First offense: up to 90 days imprisonment, $500 fine, 30 days license suspension. Subsequent offenses increase severity. | | **Right‑of‑Way / Yield Signs** | Standard right‑of‑way rules apply. At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles already in intersection. Pedestrians always have priority when crossing marked crosswalks. | Failure results in citations ($200+). | --- ### 2️⃣ Specific Road Types & Conditions | Situation | Key Laws | Practical Tips | |-----------|----------|----------------| | **School Zones** | Speed limit reduced to 25 mph during school hours (usually 7 AM–9 PM weekdays). Signage indicates times. | Keep extra eye on children; failure yields $250 fine + 2 points. | | **Construction Sites** | Follow all posted signs; often lower speed limits (15–35 mph). Workers may be present. | Slow down, stay alert, obey detour routes. | | **High‑Occupancy Vehicle (HOV)/Carpool Lanes** | Only cars with 2+ occupants (or designated carpoolers) permitted between 5:00–10:00 AM & 3:00–7:00 PM weekdays. | Check lane markings; non‑compliant vehicles get ticketed. | | **Toll Roads** | Electronic toll collection required (e.g., TxTag). Manual payment possible but slower. | Ensure tag active; avoid toll plazas to reduce congestion. | --- ### 3️⃣ Commercial Driver Regulations | Regulation | Details | |------------|---------| | **Hours of Service (HOS)** | Max 11 hrs driving per day, 14 hrs total workday, 60‑hour weekly limit. Rest periods: 34 consecutive hrs off duty each week. | Must log electronically; violations result in demerit points & potential suspensions. | | **Electronic Logging Device (ELD)** | Mandatory since 2017 for Class A/B trucks. Records HOS automatically. | Non‑compliance leads to heavy fines (~$300/hr). | | **Vehicle Weight Limits** | Varies by county; generally max 80,000 lb gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR). Overweight requires special permits. | Excess weight fines ~$150/lb over limit. | | **Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT)** | Requires DOT endorsement, proper placarding, temperature control, driver training. | Strict enforcement; severe penalties including prison time. | --- ### 4️⃣ Cyclists & Motorcyclist Rights | Issue | Law | Notes | |-------|-----|-------| | **Helmet Requirement** | Riders aged ≤18 must wear helmets. Adults optional but strongly encouraged. | Helmet law applies regardless of motorcycle class. | | **Lane Positioning** | Cyclists should travel as close to centerline as safe; may share lanes with motor vehicles. | In some counties, dedicated bike lanes exist; follow local ordinances. | | **Motorcycle Visibility** | Must keep headlights on from sunset to sunrise. | Improves detection by other motorists. | --- ### 5️⃣ Pedestrian Safety | Feature | Law | Enforcement | |--------|-----|-------------| | **Crosswalk Priority** | Pedestrians have right-of-way at marked crosswalks. | Offending drivers fined $200+. | | **Sidewalk Availability** | Municipalities must maintain sidewalks wherever feasible. | Lack of sidewalk does not absolve pedestrian liability. | | **Nighttime Lighting** | Pedestrians wearing reflective gear recommended; no legal requirement. | Helps visibility for both parties. | --- ### 6️⃣ Parking & Toll Compliance | Topic | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Parking Restrictions** | No parking within 20 ft of stop lines, fire hydrants, or curb cuts. | Violators receive tickets ($125+) and towing fees. | | **Permit Requirements** | Disabled persons require valid permit displayed. | Unlicensed disabled parking incurs hefty fines. | | **Tolls** | E-ZPass/TxTAG accepted statewide. | Cash-only options limited to select bridges/tunnels. | --- ### 7️⃣ Recent Legislative Updates (Last 24 Months) | Year | Change | Impact | |------|--------|--------| | 2024 | Increased penalty for texting while driving from $100 → $150. Added "two-point" system for repeat offenders. | Encourages stricter compliance. | | 2023 | Expanded HOV lane eligibility to electric vehicles without occupancy restrictions. | Promotes EV adoption. | | 2022 | Introduced “Safe Passage” ordinance in Austin requiring schools to install temporary barriers around construction zones near playgrounds. | Enhances student safety. | *(For full legislative history, consult the Texas Legislature website.)* --- ### 📌 Quick Reference Cheat Sheet ``` [ ] Seat Belts ✔️ [ ] Hands-Free ✅ [ ] Speed Limit ⏱️ [ ] School Zone ⚠️ [ ] Construction 🚧 [ ] HOV Lane 🛣️ [ ] Truck Hours of Service ⏰ [ ] Towing Fees 💸 [ ] Child Safety Seats 👶 [ ] Motorcycle Helmets 🎩 [ ] Crosswalk Right-of-Way 🚦 ``` --- #### Where to Find Official Sources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) Traffic Code | https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-code.html | | Texas Department of Public Safety (Driver Licensing) | https://dps.texas.gov/driver-license | | Texas Highway Patrol | https://tphp.org/ | | Texas Legislature Online (Statutes) | https://statelaw.justia.com/statutes/texas/ | Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper dives into any subsection—for example, how to file a contestable citation, or specifics on commercial truck regulations in Dallas County!
